questions.question: Let [latex]f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} [/latex] be a function such that [latex]f(x)=\max \left\{x, x^3\right\}, x \in \mathbb{R} [/latex], where [latex]\mathbb{R} [/latex] is the set of all real numbers. The set of all points where [latex]f(x) [/latex] is NOT differentiable is
questions.explanation:
Compare [latex]x[/latex] and [latex]x^3[/latex]: they are equal at [latex]x=-1,0,1[/latex]. So [latex]f(x)=x[/latex] for [latex]x\le -1[/latex], [latex]x^3[/latex] on [latex][-1,0][/latex], [latex]x[/latex] on [latex][0,1][/latex], [latex]x^3[/latex] for [latex]x\ge1[/latex].

At every switching point the two pieces have different slopes ([latex]\frac{d}{dx}x=1[/latex], [latex]\frac{d}{dx}x^3=3x^2[/latex]):
- [latex]x=-1[/latex]: slopes [latex]1[/latex] and [latex]3[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] corner
- [latex]x=0[/latex]: slopes [latex]0[/latex] and [latex]1[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] corner
- [latex]x=1[/latex]: slopes [latex]1[/latex] and [latex]3[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] corner

Everywhere else [latex]f[/latex] is a polynomial, hence differentiable.

Answer: [latex]\{-1,0,1\}[/latex]

questions.question: Consider a permutation sampled uniformly at random from the set of all permutations of [latex]\{1,2,3, \cdots, n\} [/latex] for some [latex]n \geq 4 [/latex]. Let [latex]X [/latex] be the event that 1 occurs before 2 in the permutation, and [latex]Y [/latex] the event that 3 occurs before 4 . Which one of the following statements is TRUE?

options.A: The events [latex]X [/latex] and [latex]Y [/latex] are mutually exclusive
options.D: Event [latex]X [/latex] is more likely than event [latex]Y [/latex]

questions.explanation:
By symmetry, 1 is before 2 in half of all permutations, so [latex]P(X)=\frac12[/latex]; similarly [latex]P(Y)=\frac12[/latex].

The relative order of {1,2} and the relative order of {3,4} involve different elements, and all 4 combinations (12/21 with 34/43) are equally likely, so [latex]P(X\cap Y)=\frac14=P(X)P(Y)[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] independent.

- Not mutually exclusive: 1 2 3 4 [latex]\ldots[/latex] satisfies both.
- Neither must occur: 2 1 4 3 [latex]\ldots[/latex] satisfies none.
- Equally likely, so X is not more likely than Y.

Answer: X and Y are independent

In the cycle stealing mode of DMA, one word of data is transferred between an I/O
device and main memory in a stolen cycle
options.B:
For bulk data transfer, the burst mode of DMA has a higher throughput than the
cycle stealing mode
options.C:
Programmed I/O mechanism has a better CPU utilization than the interrupt driven
I/O mechanism
options.D:
The CPU can start executing an interrupt service routine faster with vectored
interrupts than with non-vectored interrupts

- Vectored interrupts give the ISR address directly (no polling to find the device), so ISR starts faster [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.

Answer: Programmed I/O has better CPU utilization than interrupt driven I/O (FALSE)

Consider the following recurrence relation:
[latex] T(n)=\left\{\begin{array}{c} \sqrt{n} T(\sqrt{n})+n \text { for } n \geq 1, \\ 1 \quad \text { for } n=1 . \end{array}\right. [/latex]

Divide both sides by [latex]n[/latex]: [latex]\frac{T(n)}{n}=\frac{T(\sqrt n)}{\sqrt n}+1[/latex].

Let [latex]S(n)=\frac{T(n)}{n}[/latex]. Then [latex]S(n)=S(\sqrt n)+1[/latex].

Taking square roots repeatedly, [latex]n\to n^{1/2}\to n^{1/4}\to\cdots[/latex] reaches a constant after [latex]\log\log n[/latex] steps, adding 1 each step. So [latex]S(n)=\Theta(\log\log n)[/latex].

[latex]T(n)=n\,S(n)=\Theta(n\log\log n)[/latex]

Which of the following statements is/are TRUE for every such graph [latex] G [/latex] and tree [latex] T [/latex] ?
